content: PanoRef multi-origin optimizer review and follow-up. A code review of the latest implementation (span 000000–000003) rates the algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, concluding it is promising but not yet production-ready. Strengths include deterministic area-proportional sampling, full origin-evaluation criteria (occlusion, normals, viewing angle, texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, continuous quality), a genuinely joint pair mode that ranks by bitset union before tie-breakers, and a structured coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, separate fixed-first and joint branches). Blockers identified: (1) imported sets can yield zero legal candidates because clearance uses whole-object AABBs, so any origin inside the AABB is rejected; fix is actual geometry clearance via the coverage BVH with per-mesh/cluster bounds and a room-interior regression test; (2) geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports because every triangle is expanded into JS objects/arrays and 64-bit numbers, then structured-cloned to the worker, with BVH sorting of JS index arrays and per-intersection temporary array allocations causing GC pressure; fix is compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions/indices/normals, Uint32Array mesh ranges/transforms), transferable ArrayBuffers, and a flat typed-array BVH or three-mesh-bvh, avoiding per-triangle vertex expansion; (3) geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because extractCoverageScene runs synchronously before the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, transform application, disposal, and cloning freeze the UI; fix is to move extraction into the worker or chunk it with yields; (4) the UI/workflow is conceptually wrong because it writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference, which only changes metadata and projects old pixels from the wrong point, ruining alignment; correct workflow is to preserve existing panoramas, move capture origins, render new graybox panoramas, inpaint/generate styled panoramas, import them as new references, and associate each with its actual origin; (5) reachableCoverage and final combined coverage are computed on different sample banks (coarse vs fine with seed+1), so the UI can show combined coverage below reachable upper bound and reachable captured at 100%, and fixed-first excludes the fixed origin from the reachable union; fix is one shared validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, including the fixed origin for fixed-first; (6) fixed-first does not enforce minimumOriginSeparation, only filtering by object identity, so a nearly duplicate second origin can survive; add distance(first, candidate) >= minimumOriginSeparation; (7) the four-level refinement is not truly iterative because all offsets are generated around the original seed without re-centering after each level; (8) local candidates can float between floors because validation only checks that a floor exists somewhere below and offsets retain the original Y, so on sloped/multilevel sets a candidate can end up meters above a lower floor; fix is to reproject each offset onto the floor under its new X/Z at panoramaHeightMeters before clearance; (9) the optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules (optimizer uses angle/texel density, shader blends by distance), so optimized and visible results can disagree; shader should use the same approximate quality function and winner-takes-most selection. Testing assessment: current tests are good unit tests but lack the most dangerous cases—large imported room object, 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped/multilevel floors, immutable existing panorama origins, and candidate generation inside concave imported geometry—and no GitHub Actions runs are attached to the latest head, so the suite has not been independently enforced in CI. A subsequent plan (panoref_evt_000762) directs rebasing onto main, resolving the PR conflict, adding an allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering, running one real complex imported-set benchmark plus a full 100k+ optimizer integration test, and then spawning a subagent to disprove completeness and iterating until no holes remain. Implementation follow-up then aligned the runtime shader with the optimizer’s quality objective: projectedStyleMaterials.ts was patched to remove the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 constant and the projectedConfidence assertion, and to assert projectedQualityAt plus dominant-mode bias (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0) and to no longer contain projectedConfidence; the corresponding stale test in multiOriginInteraction.test.ts was replaced with an assertion protecting the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes, and the targeted regression test suite (36 tests) passed. A broader verification run then executed unit tests (42 test files, 371 tests passed, including projectionCoverage on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture, projectedStyleCompile under real WebGL with single and dual projector modes, radial-depth occlusion cubemap pixel readback, and receiving projected-style material), lint (tsc --noEmit), and build (vite build), all passing.
